Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 17 (wasp_17) directly continues the field-driven series from tutorial 16, further developing scalar-field-driven aggregation with biased-growth, isoline techniques, and parametric-growth strategies. Tutorial 16 is a direct prerequisite for tutorial 17, and the two share closely related content around field-driven discrete assembly with custom-preview and 3d-populate workflows.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 18 (wasp_18) continues the field-driven series beyond tutorial 17, confirming the series extends through at least tutorial 18. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 18 via tutorial 17.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 19 (wasp_19) continues the field-driven series beyond tutorial 18, confirming the series extends through at least tutorial 19. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 19 via tutorials 17 and 18.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 20 (wasp_20) continues the field-driven series beyond tutorial 19, confirming the series extends through at least tutorial 20. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 20 via tutorials 17, 18, and 19.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 21 (wasp_21) continues beyond tutorial 20 into a new topic series, confirming the field-driven series concludes at tutorial 20. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 21 via tutorials 17, 18, 19, and 20.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 22 (wasp_22) begins a new topic series (part-based, file-io, multi-part) that is distinct from the field-driven series (tutorials 16–20). Tutorial 21 was transitional, and tutorial 22 confirms the new series direction. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 22 via tutorials 17–21.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 23 (wasp_23) continues the new topic series (part-based, multi-part, rule-based, constraint-based) beyond tutorial 22, further confirming the field-driven series concludes at tutorial 20. Tutorial 16 is an indirect prerequisite for tutorial 23 via tutorials 17–22.

intents: create a field-driven aggregation with Wasp
use Wasp to aggregate parts along a field
generate discrete aggregation using scalar field
set up Wasp parts with connection rules and field guidance
populate space with Wasp components driven by a field
create self-organizing structure with Wasp aggregation

curriculum.text:

curriculum.title: Construct Scalar Field
curriculum.text:
3. Construct Scalar Field
Fields are used by Wasp to drive aggregations, placing new components by following
higher gradient values in the field. Field can be initialised by creating a point grid with a defined
resolution within a given bounding box.
Different Grasshopper techniques can be used to generate custom fields fit to particualt purposes
(eg. geometry reconstruction, structural performance, environmental data, attractor geometries).

NB: please be careful with setting the FieldPts resolution. If you set a very low resolution and your 
Boundaries are very large, you will quickly create millions of points, hence slowing down the whole
Grasshopper definition.

curriculum.title: Build Part
curriculum.text:
1a. Build Part
Parts are the building blocks of Wasp.
The most basic way of initializing a part is to define t he geometry (as brep or mesh),
and the connection faces (center and orientation - with a line). Parts must be named
to be identifyed in the aggregation rules.

curriculum.title: Define aggregation rules
curriculum.text:
2. Define aggregation rules
Rules can be defined ina compact way
with a text string in the format:
"Part1|Connection1_Part2|Connection2"

curriculum.title: Aggregate!
curriculum.text:
4. Aggregate!
Field Aggregation adds at every step one part that is the closest to
the highest reachable value point in the field. The component adds parts
additively over the already aggregated parts. If a new aggregation has
to be created, the RESET button allows to reset the aggregation and restart.

NB: the FieldAggregation undelying algorithm is not probabilistic, but exact.
This means that, unless you change the parts, rules, or field, you will always
get the same result from the compoent.
